column4: Making systems thinking sessions that actually work!
column5:
Systems Mapping always seem like 'the answer' for groups trying to grasp the implications of their decisions in an impossibly complex world.  Sadly. the result is often either a very pretty picture or a tangled hairball of blobs and lines.  The the impact is limited.  A senior leader in a government agency recently said to me "If one more person shows me a node and link diagram I'll scream....".

In this session we will look at the spectrum of "systems diagrams" (based on the UK Gov systems guide for Policy Makers). We will recognise key reasons why these systems exercises fail to deliver value outside the group who drew the map. We will explore what really works - all through experiencing a (small) system mapping process.

Come and play.  Go away with the starting principle you need to have a go - and lead systems sessions that actually work.

column15: I started facilitating in the 1990s doing business workshops for London Underground and have since developed my facilitation skills as part of my wider role as a management consultant.  My three most significant learngin experiences that have shaped how I facilitate today were acting as the host for a national industry group over 2 years following a major rail incident, working a facilitator for 5 years in a multi-national charity, leading groups with 10 or more nationalities and finally studying group dynamics and organisational change with a leading international group with origins in MIT.
column18: I spent 5 years working in East Asia with a multi-national organisation where we had 23 nationalities involved in the leadership groups that I had to facilitate. Depending on the mix of first languages present, I have also done sessions where some tables chose to work in a language other than English.
